definition.name: Industrial plug
definition.description: Five-pin industrial plug with separately identified contacts.

terminals.label: L1IN
terminals.purpose: Incoming L1 terminal of its separately modelled linked contact path. Pair it with L1OUT. Matching phase/neutral identities matter; mechanical linkage does not join the poles electrically.

terminals.label: L2IN
terminals.purpose: Incoming L2 terminal of its separately modelled linked contact path. Pair it with L2OUT. Matching phase/neutral identities matter; mechanical linkage does not join the poles electrically.

terminals.label: L3IN
terminals.purpose: Incoming L3 terminal of its separately modelled linked contact path. Pair it with L3OUT. Matching phase/neutral identities matter; mechanical linkage does not join the poles electrically.

terminals.label: NIN
terminals.purpose: Incoming N terminal of its separately modelled linked contact path. Pair it with NOUT. Matching phase/neutral identities matter; mechanical linkage does not join the poles electrically.

terminals.label: PE
terminals.purpose: Protective connection to the represented exposed conductive parts or protective network. It carries no intended normal load return and remains independent of switching the active conductors.

terminals.label: L1OUT
terminals.purpose: Outgoing L1 terminal of its separately modelled linked contact path. Pair it with L1IN. Matching phase/neutral identities matter; mechanical linkage does not join the poles electrically.

terminals.label: L2OUT
terminals.purpose: Outgoing L2 terminal of its separately modelled linked contact path. Pair it with L2IN. Matching phase/neutral identities matter; mechanical linkage does not join the poles electrically.

terminals.label: L3OUT
terminals.purpose: Outgoing L3 terminal of its separately modelled linked contact path. Pair it with L3IN. Matching phase/neutral identities matter; mechanical linkage does not join the poles electrically.

terminals.label: NOUT
terminals.purpose: Outgoing N terminal of its separately modelled linked contact path. Pair it with NIN. Matching phase/neutral identities matter; mechanical linkage does not join the poles electrically.

terminals.label: PEOUT
terminals.purpose: Outgoing protective connection to the represented exposed conductive parts or protective network. It carries no intended normal load return and remains independent of switching the active conductors.

parts.name: Housing
parts.purpose: The enclosure supports and separates functional parts. This original teaching model is representative equipment, not a manufacturer drawing.

parts.name: Removable cover
parts.purpose: The cover limits access to internal connections. Opening it here is a virtual inspection operation.

parts.name: Terminal clamps
parts.purpose: Metal clamps establish connections to individual conductors. The circuit engine connects terminal IDs, not the apparent proximity of 3D wires.

parts.name: Mounting and fixings
parts.purpose: Mounting hardware supports the equipment. Screws, rail clips and glands are modelled separately from electrical connections.

parts.name: Contact pins
parts.purpose: Pins and socket contacts have distinct identities. Matching physical equipment alone does not verify conductor assignment.

parts.name: Cable sheath and individual cores
parts.purpose: The sheath provides mechanical protection around individual insulated conductors. Identification helps reading a circuit but does not prove that a conductor has been connected correctly.
